provenance.paper_title: Benchmarking the computational power of quantum computers
provenance.page_convention: One-based PDF pages equal printed pages. Equation and section numbers are from this version.
provenance.method: Read local PDF text and read-only reference source; no numerical digitization of plots.
provenance.numeric_policy: Retain printed precision; null means not stated or unresolved, not zero. Derived quantities are identified separately.

circuit_family.width: w computational qubits; separate from physical qubit budget and ancillas

cnot_layer.connectivity: all-to-all in the uncompiled benchmark circuit
cnot_layer.sampling: Independent uniform matching in each layer; for odd w omit a uniformly random qubit.
cnot_layer.control_target: SI II.B states uniform pairings; SI VI.A.4 explicitly describes uniform ordered control-target pairs. No sampler pseudocode is supplied.

circuit_family.order: CNOT layer then independent rotation layer; repeat m=d/2 times
circuit_family.individual_layer_depth: d=2m is even and counts the uncompiled CNOT and rotation layers, not compiled hardware depth

final_layer.selection: Uniform random k-qubit subset; apply same matching and rotation sampling on that subset.

circuit_family.admissibility: Only sizes generated by the exact counts are benchmark shapes. Not every integer s is allowed.

compilation.first_stage: Architecture-specific exact or approximate compilation, including routing and ancillas; compare to original target unitary and charge approximation error.
compilation.mirror_stage: Exact lowering with barriers needed to preserve MCFE assumptions.

even_width_even_final_subset.condition: w and k both even, including partial final layers
even_width_even_final_subset.note: s=w*d still requires a full final layer k=w.

success_metric.process_fidelity: F_e=<Phi|[((Lambda o U_dagger) tensor I)(|Phi><Phi|)]|Phi>, where |Phi> is maximally entangled on two w-qubit registers
success_metric.global_depolarizing_case: If Lambda=D_p o U and D_p(rho)=p*rho+(1-p)*I/2^w, gamma=p; p is not F_e.
success_metric.spam: Exclude initial preparation and final measurement of computational qubits; include mid-circuit preparation/measurement and QEC errors.

test.sigma: Hierarchical nonparametric bootstrap over sampled circuits and shots, including SPAM references.
test.alternative: Paper also permits the 5th bootstrap percentile instead of the normal approximation.

score_confidence.guarantee: Pr(Q_hat > Q) <= 0.05 under the test assumptions
score_confidence.procedure: Choose an increasing-size in-cone sequence before inspecting its test outcomes; test each at 0.05 and stop on the first failure; report last pass or zero.
score_confidence.adaptive_note: Predictable choices based on independent prior data and fresh tests are allowed; do not reorder from the same observed test data. SI IV.D.4 also supplies significance wagering.
score_confidence.allowed_alternatives: Methods p7 permits any procedure guaranteeing at least 95% score confidence, unless a different confidence is stated; gated tests are the paper implementation, not the only admissible protocol.

region_confidence.method: Score family at 0.05 plus Hochberg tests for extra shapes at familywise 0.05; Bonferroni is an alternative. Downward closure needs monotonic mean polarization.
region_confidence.allowed_alternatives: Methods p7 permits any procedure guaranteeing at least 90% region confidence, unless otherwise stated.

success_metric.statistical_scope: Confidence addresses sampling uncertainty, not bias from invalid MCFE assumptions or extrapolation models.

mirror_protocol.composition_order: Matrix order: rightmost factor acts first.
mirror_protocol.wrappers: L consists of iid uniform single-qubit Cliffords; L_prime inverts L up to a random local Pauli, giving a known deterministic output bitstring.
mirror_protocol.effective_polarization_estimator: lambda_hat=(4^w*sum_{j=0}^w[(-1/2)^j*h_hat_j]-1)/(4^w-1), with h_hat_j the fraction at Hamming distance j from the known target.
mirror_protocol.identical_reference_case: If g=g_ref, omit a separate M2 sample and use gamma_hat=sqrt(lambda_bar_1/lambda_bar_3). H2 describes the retained identical ensemble as M2.

generic_counts.note: K, L1, L2, L3 and kappa follow SI IV.C notation; platform sections reuse K/kappa differently.

mirror_protocol.doubling: Forward plus inverse-reference circuit: approximately twice forward size/depth plus wrappers, compilation and other overhead; not a universal exact factor of two in wall time.
assumptions: Reference errors approximately stochastic with approximately equal forward/inverse polarization.
Pooled estimator neglects a covariance term and approximates mean versus RMS; paper notes a usually small optimistic bias.
Mirroring an approximate synthesis alone can cancel its coherent error; synthesis must be charged separately.

logical_helios_variant.estimator: gamma_bar >= approximately sqrt(E[lambda(M)]) (Eq. 52), without SPAM division
logical_helios_variant.synthesis_charge: Insert stochastic logical Paulis implementing a depolarizing channel whose process infidelity equals the synthesized rotation process infidelity.
logical_helios_variant.conditions: Approximately error-free logical Paulis, MCFE/local-to-global and mean/RMS approximations; this is an approximate conservative bound.

Willow_rate.note: The paragraph says 25 QUOPS circuits with 500k shots each; it does not separately enumerate the resulting M1/M2 count.

Boston.shots_citation: SI IX.D p43 explicitly states K=1000; IX.B p42 gives circuit/reference counts.

H2.SPAM_reuse_ambiguity: Table IV says extra 2000 SPAM shots for each point; SI VII.D.2 says one ensemble for each width.

experimental_counts.Helios_logical: See per_shape.logical_helios; v2/v3 redraw the circuit per shot, v1 uses multiple shots per structure.

score_and_rate.report_shape: Report width w_Q and rate at the score-maximizing shape, not independently the shape of maximum rate.
score_and_rate.counts: N_total=N_kept+N_reject over M1/M2 circuit executions; without postselection sqrt(N_total*N_kept)=N_total.
score_and_rate.wall_time: Elapsed first-to-last mirror execution, including unavoidable circuit changes, readout/reset, recalibration and replenishment; separable queue and transfer delays may be excluded. M3 time may be excluded.
score_and_rate.postselection_caveat: Square-root survival correction approximates equal rejection probability in the two mirror halves; a better scheme-specific mapping may replace it. Early-abort cost belongs in elapsed time.

error_mitigated.score: Q_star_alpha uses same cone with gamma_bar>=alpha
error_mitigated.meaning: Potential error-mitigation capability, not applying unheralded-error mitigation to QUOPS data; overhead is approximate and omits noise-learning costs and possible estimator bias.

score_and_rate.units: Scores count weighted uncompiled universal operations; rates are QUOPS per second.
score_and_rate.optional_pairs: Methods p8 also permits reporting score/rate pairs from other in-cone capability points; the headline maximum score should carry the rate at its own shape.

error_mitigated_headline.evidence: Measured data plus model extrapolation; not a direct demonstrated score at every shape. Width not numerically stated alongside these scores.

extrapolation_method.fit: Gaussian likelihood for gamma_hat with bootstrap sigma_s; constrained maximum likelihood r_w in [0,1].
extrapolation_method.confidence: Paper uses 2[ell(r_hat)-ell(r_upper)]<chi2(1,0.95) and calls r_upper a one-sided 95% bound; region exp(-r_upper*s)>alpha.
extrapolation_method.rate: Raw rate measured at the standard-score shape times exp(-2*r_hat_w*Q_star_alpha).
extrapolation_method.limitations: Exponential decay and negligible raw-rate shape dependence are heuristic; no universal compilation theorem gives either. Confidence is model-conditional.

per_shape.source_policy: Transcription of Tables IV-VI. Preserve pass markers, missing values and malformed entries rather than reconstructing them. Durations converted to seconds. Some sampled shapes lie outside the score cone.

physical_h2.source_anomaly: Printed postselected CI is [0.8301]] and postselected pass is a dash; upper endpoint left null. SI VII.B says leakage detection is used only for w<56, conflicting with this row.

google_and_ibm.location: Fig. 17 p44 plots per-shape mean polarization and one-sigma error bars. Numeric point coordinates are not tabulated. No digitized values are represented as exact.

logical_helios_details.fault_tolerance: v1/v2 use individually fault-tolerant gadgets but not a fully composable distance-three circuit; v3 uses frame tracking, correlated Steane QEC and strict resource preparation to ensure no single circuit fault causes logical failure.
logical_helios_details.QEC: v1/v2 flag QEC after rotations containing T and after CNOT; v3 QEC before operations only when the tracked error frame requires it, with parallel resource preparation and injection/QEC merging.
logical_helios_details.magic: RUS verified encoded magic states, maximum three attempts; no shots discarded in the reported logical experiments.

architecture_specific.source: SI VII.C.7 p37; compiled gate counts estimated from 100000 Cliffordized simulations, not extracted from experimental shot logs.

Willow.rate_experiment: Includes classical control, waveform compilation, readout/reset and a small number of M3 circuits; excludes interleaved other-user jobs.

Boston.experimental_rate: Mixed-shape batches prevent exact per-shape timing; uses batch raw rate and reported QPU usage time (smaller than full job elapsed time).
Boston.ambiguities: SI IX.D prose says multiply raw rate by polarization, whereas normative Eq.72 and Eq.109 use polarization squared. Eq.107 omits an explicit shot multiplicity; do not infer a complete execution census from it.

Quantinuum.timing: Timed shapes use reserved windows and first-shot start to last-shot finish, including ordinary overhead. Starred logical timings are from normal operation; untimed points ran through the ordinary interleaved queue.

timing.unresolved: p27 defines L in logical timesteps of d_code cycles, so p29 appears to omit d_code unless t_cyc is reinterpreted.

operations.CNOT: lattice surgery with ancilla volume for computational patches in a line

error_model.interpretation: No-fault proxy compared directly with the polarization threshold.
error_model.p_cyc: Logical error per cycle imported from FLASQ; paper does not supply a closed distance law or its fit constants.

planar_surface_code.synthesis: pygridsynth (GridSynth); quadratic process-infidelity charge eps_rot^2, assuming coherent synthesis errors combine incoherently. N_rot=s/2 is the projection approximation, exact only for dense even shapes.

sampling.gate_counts: Multiply sampled mean H/S/Sdag/T cost by estimated rotations; use uniform ordered-pair CNOT counts.
sampling.distance_choice: First odd distance whose proxy passes, otherwise maximum proxy over scan; average over ten circuits and require >1/sqrt(e).

missing_inputs: Per-gate ancilla-volume dictionary and logical error/cultivation curves inherited from Ref.36, not reproduced numerically.
Exact numerical projected rates are plotted in Fig.2f, not tabulated.
planar_surface_code.size_ceiling_wording: SI VI.A says O(1e6) sizes limited by cultivation; main text p5 says capability regions cut off around 1e7. These are approximate, differently phrased limits, not an exact universal cap.

all_to_all.cycle_definition: Worst-case all-qubit pairing, 2q gates between 1q layers, possibly followed by measurement/reset; fixed 10 ms even though transport is expected to scale with sqrt(nq).

csd.intrablock_SWAP_transversal: physical 1q Clifford gates and relabeling, treated as depth zero

all_to_all.magic: fold-transversal surface-code cultivation for both code families
all_to_all.decoding_assumption: Scalable correlated decoding permits one syndrome round per logical gadget rather than O(d_code).
all_to_all.scheduler: Unpublished Ref.97 tracks lifetimes, dynamic state preparation, failed attempts, corrections, idling and EC scheduling.
all_to_all.synthesis: Same pygridsynth square-root precision as planar case; one-third synthesis budget, remaining two-thirds flexible between QEC and magic.

fit_model.notation: m replaces paper section VI.B d, which denotes benchmark-layer count here. Time parameters are depth-1 cycles.
fit_model.missing: Fitted effective error and timing parameters and per-code EC error curves are not numerically tabulated.

method.synthesis_type: Mixed fallback (Kliuchnikov et al.), a stochastic synthesis model; distinct from deterministic pygridsynth used for device projections.
ignored: 4/3 polarization versus process-infidelity factor (paper says approximately 1% effect on target)
method.target_rate: Q_target/per_execution_time, a raw rate; comparing to polarization-attenuated reported Omega is conservative by up to e.

rows.note: Per-shot count derived in paper from 6.5e9 total Toffolis / 9.2 expected runs.
Five-day budget is chosen here for comparison, not a runtime supplied by the chemistry resource estimate.

historical_qv_inferences.evidence: Approximate conversions of quantum-volume measurements, not directly measured QUOPS. QV width is not an identified QUOPS maximizing width. Rates are not supplied. Printed rounding retained.

reference_code_audit.finding: Arbitrary Pauli rotations and nonlocal CNOT counts match the intended primitives; count-only CircuitSpec does not sample axes, angles or matchings.
Docstring describes rotation plus CNOT; normative paper is CNOT then rotation. Count-only object encodes no order.
s=N_R+2*N_CNOT matches the paper, but returned counts need not have the requested s.
floor(w/2) is correct for full layers. w/2 and 2w per benchmark layer require even width; final partial layer is absent.
round(s/(2w)) loses partial layers and miscounts odd widths. depth=2D is correct only for its represented full layers, not generally the requested shape.
Default inclusive exponents 2 and 3 match; changing them defines a different benchmark.
alpha=1/sqrt(e) matches; lower alpha is allowed if overhead and rate are reported.
F must be ensemble process polarization, not entanglement fidelity or a single-circuit success probability. Global depolarizing parameter can equal gamma, but is a modeling assumption.
Point F>=alpha has no one-sided confidence bound, bootstrap, mirror estimator or finite-circuit uncertainty; usable only as a declared deterministic projection.
30 mirrors x 100 shots = 3000 is not a paper requirement or a demonstrated-platform default.
Factor two reflects forward/inverse mirroring but omits wrapper, reference-ensemble, SPAM and circuit-change costs.
One week (604800 s) to complete the test is an added study constraint; the paper has no universal one-week pass criterion.
Multiplying baseline test shots by 1/F^2 below the default alpha is a runtime-model choice. Paper overhead concerns extracting mitigated observables, not a prescribed MCFE shot requirement.
s*F^2/t_shot matches foundational rate if F is mean gamma and t_shot is representative accepted-forward time. Real operational rate uses measured mirror wall time.
Dividing time and multiplying rate by copies assumes independent simultaneous executions with linear throughput scaling; must include device-wide overhead in an operational measurement.
No acceptance/rejection counts or durations and no sqrt(N_total*N_kept) term. Valid only without postselection or if an equivalent accepted-time model is already incorporated.
Widths 3 through 4000 are a search restriction; the paper permits widths 1 and 2 and does not prescribe a 4000 cap.
Forty rounded geometric s values are a coarse search choice; some are inadmissible discrete shapes and better feasible sizes can be missed.
Reports largest nominal passing s and its width/rate rather than independently maximizing rate; subject to the count and search issues.
Stopping an ascending size scan assumes a monotone model; paper gated statistics is one preselected increasing-size sequence with confidence tests, not nested point-estimate scans.
Breaking on low-size execution infeasibility assumes all larger widths infeasible; an architecture returning None can also reflect synthesis/factory constraints. Not a benchmark definition.
No paper rule says three unsuccessful widths rule out all larger widths.
Integer steps below 32 and ~15% thereafter can skip the optimum; not a paper sampling rule.
Approximation must consume success budget. This principle matches, but does not make the downstream numerical FT model the paper model.

Default 3*log2(1/eps), eps=0.4*(1-alpha)/N_R and linear N_R*eps are not SI VI pygridsynth square-root precision with quadratic charge and a one-third synthesis budget. If eps is intended as infidelity, the Ross-Selinger cost needs that convention made explicit.

Surface p=0.001 and 1 us cycle match the planar example, but A=0.1, threshold=0.01, d<=61, patch multiplier, distillation factories, 40/30/30 budgets and timing optimization are study assumptions, not the QUOPS projection specification.
NISQ F includes terminal measurement infidelity; QUOPS computational process polarization removes terminal SPAM (while rate includes readout time).

ambiguities_and_limits.finding: SI II.B/ Fig.4 is CNOT then rotation. SI IV.B.3 explicitly adopts the reverse order for its derivation; VI.B and Table V count benchmark layers as depth. Use m for benchmark layers and d_code for code distance.
The projection uses N_R=s/2 even at reported odd widths 13,21,41; exact family counts differ. Preserve this approximation when reproducing the projection, but use Eqs.9-10 for the benchmark.
A logical timestep is d_code syndrome cycles (p27), yet p29 gives t_cyc*L with t_cyc=1 us. The factor of d_code is unresolved in the paper text.

Neither a complete numerical logical-distance law nor the all-to-all fitted parameter tables are supplied; external FLASQ inputs and unpublished scheduler details are needed for a full numerical reproduction.

SI IX.D prose says polarization rather than polarization squared; Eq.107 does not explicitly show shot multiplicity. Normative Eqs.72/109 use gamma squared. Report the published rate without silently reconciling these statements.
At (56,224), a malformed postselected interval and numeric leakage data coexist with a missing pass marker and text saying leakage detection was restricted to w<56.
Table IV says 2000 extra SPAM shots per point; VII.D.2 describes one SPAM ensemble per width. Sharing/execution count is not completely unambiguous.
Willow/Boston per-shape polarizations and some projected widths/rates are graph-only, without exact numerical tables. They are null here, not guessed from pixels.
Use Eqs.5-6 for unambiguous entanglement-fidelity normalization; the trace notation in Eq.7/main Eq.1 does not spell out its normalization.
Operational Eq.62 uses >=, while some prose/captions say exceeds or >. This transcription adopts >= for the formal test; no listed result is exactly on the boundary.
The mean-polarization estimator is approximate and can be slightly optimistic (Eq.59 discussion); confidence bounds do not remove model bias.
SI XI.C writes F=gamma+(1-gamma)/2^n while SI I.B process fidelity uses 4^n. Historical tables are retained as printed, not recomputed using a silently corrected convention.

validation.limitations: Verification of published numbers and definitions; not a reproduction of experiments or full external FT resource-estimation pipelines.

data_availability.paper_statement: Experimental/simulated data and associated code are promised for public release before publication at PRAQTICE.
data_availability.check_scope: Default-branch recursive path listing; no path containing QUOPS, Willow, Boston or Helios. The capability-learning folder identifies a different paper.
data_availability.conclusion: No identifiable QUOPS data package found in this bounded check; graph-only exact values remain unspecified. This does not assert absence on all branches or other repositories.
